name: Alprazolam
summary: A fast-onset, short-acting benzodiazepine for panic and anxiety — effective short-term but with the highest abuse and withdrawal risk of the class.
mechanism: Positive allosteric modulation of GABA-A receptors, enhancing inhibitory GABAergic transmission.

dosing.adult: 0.25–0.5 mg up to three times daily; panic disorder often 0.5–1 mg TID
dosing.maxDose: 4 mg/day (rarely up to 10 mg/day per label)

safety.pregnancy: Avoid; late-pregnancy use is linked to floppy infant syndrome and neonatal withdrawal.
safety.lactation: Enters breast milk; infant sedation possible.
contraindications: Severe respiratory insufficiency or sleep apnea
warnings: Boxed warning: dependence, abuse, and severe withdrawal (including seizures) with abrupt cessation
Boxed warning: respiratory depression when combined with opioids
Falls and cognitive impairment, especially in the elderly
Highest abuse liability among common benzodiazepines (fast onset, short half-life)
monitoring: Signs of dependence or dose escalation
Respiratory status if opioids are involved
safety.overdose: Sedation and respiratory depression (especially with alcohol or opioids); flumazenil can reverse, with seizure risk.

clinicalPearls: Fastest onset and shortest duration of the common benzodiazepines — the hardest to stop; taper very slowly.
CYP3A4 substrate — azole antifungals and grapefruit can markedly raise levels.
good: Short-term panic or anxiety relief when rapid onset is needed — with a clear plan to limit duration.
bad: Long-term use, substance-use history, older adults, or concurrent opioids.
